deviations: Restriction in the design (Language Fluency None never paired with Origin 'Another region in your country') is not modelled with an interaction; AMCEs come from a plain OLS with main-effect dummies for all seven attributes. Reason for migration is unrestricted, so its AMCEs are unaffected in expectation.

Sample: Qualtrics survey-preview responses (DistributionChannel 'preview') dropped; every profile pair with a non-missing forced choice kept, including respondents who did not finish all nine tasks. Respondent and choice-task counts are computed from this estimation sample.
notes: attempt-1 was exploratory (no RESULT lines): inspected the Qualtrics conjoint exports (F-k-j attribute names, F-k-p-j levels, forced choice in force_choice and Q184..Q198). Final: reshaped the U.S. and German conjoint CSVs to one row per profile (two per pair), outcome = profile chosen in the forced choice, German levels translated to English via the conjoint_design .dat files (Atheist mapped to the Agnostic baseline). OLS with fixest, all seven attributes, baselines economic opportunity / no language / female / unemployed / agnostic(atheist) / another region / no vulnerability, SEs clustered by respondent (ResponseId). Respondents = distinct respondents contributing at least one choice; choice tasks = profiles in the estimation. No script files in the dataset were opened; only data files were read. In reading the paper's method section I incidentally saw text values that were not withheld (e.g. U.S. wildfires about 4 points, German wildfires about 6 points, two Table 2 vulnerability rows); the specification was fixed in advance and not tuned toward them.
